neighbours.label: article after 'is' / 'as' that assigns someone an identity or role in a theological or philosophical claim ('Moses is the author', 'God as the eternal Being')
fire: Most scholars accept that Luke is the author of the book of Acts.
In Aquinas, God is understood as the first cause of all motion.
For Descartes, the thinking self stands as an independent substance.
The prophet is presented as the messenger of a covenant with Israel.
Christians confess that Christ is the mediator between God and man.
Kant treats the moral agent as a rational lawgiver to itself.
Tradition holds that David is the composer of many of the psalms.
The Stoics regarded reason as the guiding principle of the cosmos.
quiet: Most scholars accept that Luke wrote the book of Acts as well.
In Aquinas, God first causes all motion in the created world.
For Descartes, the thinking self exists independently of the body.
The prophet delivers a covenant message to the people of Israel.
Christians confess that Christ mediates between God and man.
Kant argues that the moral agent gives itself rational laws.
Tradition holds that David composed many of the psalms himself.
The Stoics believed reason guides the whole of the cosmos.

notes: Card: top peaks are ' the' / ' an' / ' a' after 'is' or 'as' in claims like 'Moses is the responsible author', 'Jesus is the great law giver', 'himself as an autonomous knower', 'God as the eternal omnipresent Being'. Quiet items make the same claims with a verb instead of 'is/as + article'.
